attempts.label: DANDI:001773
attempts.paper_title: Deep brain stimulation induces white matter remodeling and functional changes to brain-wide networks
attempts.entry_title: White matter remodeling and network changes after SCC-DBS in macaques (Fujimoto et al. 2026)
attempts.summary: Most main findings hold up in this data: stimulation raised fractional anisotropy in the mid-cingulate bundle, increased myelinating oligodendrocytes with thicker myelin, lowered cortical and raised subcortical connectivity, and reduced subgenual cingulate connectivity with default mode, limbic and executive networks. In the implanted but unstimulated monkey, the opposite fractional anisotropy decrease also reproduced. The nonsurgical controls' lack of change, the local increase at the implant site and the network-sorted connectivity plot could not be tested, because whole-brain maps, control seed data and ROI names are missing. The connectivity results assume the deposited maps are those the paper analysed. One minor claim failed: that monkey's foraging fell, and the paper reports no test for it.
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Fujimoto, Fujimoto, Elorette et al. (2026) on dandiset 001773, which holds the paper's derived values (voxel FA, voxel seed connectivity, group connectomes, CC1 and DAPI counts, EM g-ratios, home-cage behavior bins) and its MATLAB scripts. It repeats the paper's ANOVAs, Tukey-Kramer tests and rank-sum tests for the stimulated monkeys N and T, the lead-implanted monkey D and the nonsurgical controls. The whole-brain voxel maps and the controls' seed connectivity are not in the dandiset.

outcomes.statement: After 6 weeks of SCC-DBS, monkeys N and T spent more time moving and more time foraging in the home cage than before, in the same direction in both animals.
outcomes.source: Results, SCC-DBS induces selective macroscale remodeling in the CB, paragraph 1; Extended Data Fig. 1

statistics.n: 120 pre and 120 post 10-s bins, monkeys N and T

statistics.test: one-way ANOVA, monkey as fixed effect
statistics.n: 120 pre and 120 post 10-s bins, monkeys N and T

outcomes.notes: Under reading (a), the FigE1 script's model (monkey, condition and their interaction), condition gives F(1,236) = 34.61, P = 1.4e-08, partial eta squared 0.128 for movement and F(1,236) = 17.35, P = 4.4e-05, 0.068 for foraging. Reading (b) gives F 33.81 and 16.46, both P below 1e-04. The post probability is higher in N (movement 0.083 to 0.550, foraging 0.033 to 0.050) and in T (0.200 to 0.383, 0.017 to 0.300).
deviations: The foraging values are read as 1 yes and 0 no, as for movement; the sheet's legend says yes 2 and no 1, which no value uses.

outcomes.statement: In the unstimulated lead-implanted monkey D, the amount of movement and foraging did not change between before and 6 weeks after implantation.
outcomes.source: Results, The impact of SCC-DBS lead insertion on functional and structural brain networks, paragraph 2; Extended Data Fig. 1 (monkey D)
outcomes.quote: First, there was no change in the amount of movement or foraging in naturalistic behavior
outcomes.notes: By the criterion's test, a one-way ANOVA of monkey D's 120 bins on condition, movement does not differ (0.383 pre, 0.267 post, F(1,118) = 1.86, P = 0.175) but foraging does (11 of 60 bins before, 3 of 60 after, 0.183 to 0.050, F(1,118) = 5.32, P = 0.023; Fisher exact P = 0.043). The paper reports no test for monkey D (its Extended Data Fig. 1 legend analyses only N and T), so the test is the claims file's reading of the Methods applied to one animal. The deposited FigE1 script (135 lines) runs its only test calls, anovan (lines 18 and 19) and multcompare (24 and 26), on the rows of group 1 (N and T); monkey D's rows (monkey 3, group 2) enter only the means, standard errors and sample sizes of lines 35 to 125. The deposited script therefore runs no test for monkey D. The change in monkey D is a decrease, opposite to the increase of the DBS animals.
deviations: The paper reports no test for monkey D; the criterion applies the Methods' ANOVA to its bins.

outcomes.statement: After 6 weeks of SCC-DBS, fractional anisotropy (FA) increased in the cingulum bundle of the stimulated hemisphere, with a significant PrePost x side interaction and a significant pre against post difference in the stimulated CB.

outcomes.quote: We found there was a selective increase in FA in the CB in the stimulated hemisphere, particularly the mid-cingulate portion, after 6 weeks of SCC-DBS

statistics.n: voxels pooled over N and T; stimulated CB 380, UF 252, FM 105; control CB 363, UF 367, FM 133; each pre and post

outcomes.notes: With the Fig2A script's model (monkey, and PrePost, side and tract with all their interactions; type III), PrePost x side F(1,3187) = 4.64, P = 0.031, partial eta squared 0.0015. deviations: The model terms and the Tukey-Kramer family (the 12 PrePost x side x tract cells) are those of the paper's Fig2A script in the dandiset (`anovan` with `model_mat2`, `multcompare` with Dimension [2 3 4]), which the claims file left to the code. outcomes.statement: After SCC-DBS, whole-brain functional connectivity between cortical areas decreased and connectivity between subcortical areas increased.
outcomes.source: Results, Whole-brain functional connectivity changes following SCC-DBS, paragraph 1; Fig. 4a top right, Fig. 4b top
outcomes.quote: Broadly, we observed a reduction in cortico–cortical functional connectivity and a concurrent increase in subcortico–subcortical functional connectivity
outcomes.notes: In the deposited DBS group difference connectome (123 ROIs, cortical the first 54 as in the Fig. 4 script) the cortical block mean is -0.096 and the subcortical block mean +0.012 (reading (a)); the median ROI change is -0.052 over cortical ROIs and +0.006 over subcortical ROIs (reading (b)). 78% of cortical and 40% of subcortical entries are negative.
deviations: The connectome is the group average the dandiset holds, not recomputed from runs; its ROIs have no names, and the cortical block is taken from the Fig. 4 script (first 54 ROIs).

outcomes.statement: Per ROI, functional connectivity changed significantly between pre and post scans in 69 of the 123 CHARM and SARM ROIs in the DBS group and in 44 of 123 in the nonsurgical control group.
outcomes.source: Fig. 4b and legend; Supplementary Tables 1 and 2
outcomes.inferred: The counts are the number of ROIs listed in Supplementary Tables 1 (DBS group) and 2 (nonsurgical control group), the ROIs significant in Fig. 4b; no sentence states them.
outcomes.notes: Under the amended criterion, the paper's Fig. 4 script's test (rank-sum of each ROI's 122 off-diagonal changes against 122 zeros, significant at P < 0.05/123), computed as MATLAB's ranksum (tie and continuity corrected), gives 69 ROIs for the DBS group (41 of 54 cortical, 28 of 69 subcortical) and 44 for the controls, the reported counts, with or without the diagonal. The largest P counted is 3.88e-04 in both groups, the largest value listed in Supplementary Tables 1 and 2 (3.9e-4). Of the variants, the same test at the Methods' threshold 0.01/123 gives 62 and 36, the pre against post rank-sum 10 to 44 (DBS) and 4 to 15 (controls), and the signed-rank of the changes 60 to 85 and 27 to 49. What the answer changed. The earlier criterion named only the pre against post rank-sum and the signed-rank, at 0.01/122 or 0.01, none of which puts both counts in tolerance, so the outcome rested on an assumption that the script's test and threshold are the paper's (reproduced, assumed). The reader's answer of 2026-11-03 (questions/001773.yaml) made the script's test and threshold the criterion and changed the statement's 122 ROIs to 123. The outcome stays reproduced, the counts are the same, and it no longer rests on an assumption.
deviations: The matrices have 123 ROIs, so each ROI has 122 values, the n of the legend; the threshold uses 123 as the script and the amended criterion do (0.01/122 is also shown).

outcomes.statement: Sorted by cortical network membership, functional connectivity within and across networks was reduced after SCC-DBS.
outcomes.source: Results, Whole-brain functional connectivity changes following SCC-DBS, paragraph 1; Fig. 4c left
outcomes.quote: When the functional connectivity was sorted based on cortical networks membership, it was clear that connectivity within and across networks was reduced
outcomes.notes: The criterion blocks the claim without an assignment of the connectome's ROIs to networks. The reader's answer of 2026-11-03 changed the criterion's 122 ROIs to 123, the number the deposited connectomes have; this does not change the block. The dandiset's connectomes (123 x 123) have no ROI names, the Fig. 4 script reads the names from atlas key files that are not deposited (CHARM_key_4.txt, SARM_key_4.txt, reorder_rois.txt), and neither the script nor the paper assigns ROIs to the networks of Fig. 4c. The deposited circular plot sheet holds the 54 x 54 cortical block of each group's difference without network labels. The notebook prints the script's lines that read labels or draw the circular plot (one colour for decreases, one for increases, no grouping) and every text cell of the workbook (block titles only). Supplementary Tables 3 and 4 name the ROIs but give no network.

outcomes.statement: In the nonsurgical control animals, scans 6 to 7 weeks apart showed no systematic pattern of functional connectivity change.
outcomes.source: Results, Whole-brain functional connectivity changes following SCC-DBS, paragraph 1; Fig. 4a,b bottom, Fig. 4c right
outcomes.quote: In these control animals, a comparison conducted between scans acquired 6–7 weeks apart did not reveal a systematic pattern of functional changes
outcomes.notes: In the controls' difference connectome the cortical block mean is +0.001 and the subcortical -0.004 (reading (a)), the ROI medians +0.001 and -0.001 (reading (b)), so the DBS pattern is absent under both; against DBS values -0.096, +0.012, -0.052 and +0.006. 49% of the controls' cortical entries are negative (DBS 78%). Under the script's per-ROI test the controls have 44 significant ROIs, as the paper lists.

outcomes.statement: Before stimulation, the SCC was positively connected with vmFC, dACC, PCC, STG, hippocampus, amygdala and DLPFC, and negatively with the insula and somatosensory cortex.
outcomes.source: Results, Whole-brain functional connectivity changes following SCC-DBS, paragraph 2; Fig. 5a top row; Extended Data Fig. 7 top row
outcomes.quote: Before stimulation, the SCC showed positive connectivity to the ventromedial frontal cortex (vmFC), dorsal anterior cingulate cortex (dACC), posterior cingulate cortex (PCC), superior temporal gyrus (STG), hippocampus (HIP), amygdala (AMY) and dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC), as well as negative connectivity to the insula and somatosensory cortex
outcomes.notes: Before DBS, in the stimulated hemisphere, vmFC 0.123, STG 0.099, DLPFC 0.066, dACC 0.064, AMY 0.042, HIP 0.038 and PCC 0.038 are positive, the anterior-dorsal insula -0.013 and the somatosensory cortex -0.026 negative; 9 of 9 signs match, and 9 of 9 with both hemispheres pooled. Each sign is the same in N and T separately.
deviations: The deposited seed tables hold one value per voxel and session (column date), and the paper's scripts analyse them as they are. The paper does not say whether a session's map comes from concatenated runs or from per-run maps averaged; the file name's "concatenated" may refer to runs or to subjects and ROIs combined in one sheet. Only this one version is deposited, so only one of the criterion's two run readings is run.

Assumed that the deposited seed maps, one per session, are the maps the paper analysed. The paper leaves open whether runs were concatenated or averaged, and only one version is deposited, so only one run reading can be run. The interaction F values match the reported ones (186.48, 51.09, 7.36, 4.58), which supports it.

In those ROIs the sham-side area 25 has the largest increase (+0.18, P = 4.3e-12 in the 17-ROI model, printed under ed10d-monkey-d-roi-changes). The readings disagree (reproduced only for the sham side with the script's LIM), and the criterion blocks the claim when they do. The question for the paper's authors is whether "not observed" covers the control hemisphere, where their own legend lists a significant CEN difference (the data show a decrease), and the script settles LIM as including area 25. The Fig. 6e legend's LIM voxel counts (438 sham, 383 control) are those with area 25 (428 and 375 without), so the paper's n support reading (a); a reader is asked whether reading (b) should stay (questions/001773.yaml). deviations: Assumed that the deposited seed maps, one per session, are the maps the paper analysed. The paper leaves open whether runs were concatenated or averaged, and only one version is deposited, so only one run reading can be run. The interaction F values match the reported ones (186.48, 51.09, 7.36, 4.58), which supports it.

findings.statement: The Data availability statement says the functional MRI data are deposited in this dandiset, but it holds only derived values (seed connectivity of the voxels of 17 target ROIs for monkeys N, T and D, and three group-average connectomes). There are no fMRI or DWI images, no whole-brain seed maps, no seed connectivity for the nonsurgical controls B, W and H, and no per-monkey connectomes, so the voxelwise cluster maps of Fig. 5a, Fig. 6d and Extended Data Figs. 7, 8 and 10d cannot be tested.

The connectomes in "Source Data FC matrix.xlsx" (123 x 123) carry no ROI names. The Fig. 4 script reads them from atlas key and reorder files (CHARM_key_4.txt, SARM_key_4.txt, reorder_rois.txt) that are not deposited, so no ROI can be named and the network sorting of Fig. 4c cannot be repeated.

The legend in dbs_behavior_data_a.xlsx codes foraging as yes 2 and no 1, but every foraging value is 0 or 1; read as 1 yes, the values give the paper's statistics. The same legend gives group codes 1 (DBS) and 0 (non-stimulation control), while monkey D's rows carry group 2.

In CC1_MCC_CB_data_a.xlsx two fields of monkey T's control side (section T423, fields 3 and 4) carry CC1/DAPI ratios that do not match their counts (44.9 and 35.4 % against 35.4 and 44.2 % from the counts); field 4's ratio is field 3's. Two MCC-CB fields have more CC1-positive than DAPI-positive cells (ratio above 100 %). The paper's script uses the ratio column; with the ratio from the counts the side effect changes from F = 9.00 to 9.03.

In dbs_EMgratio_MCC_CB_data_a.xlsx the column headed "diameter of axon(pixel)" holds half the mean of the long and short diameters (a radius), and "diameter of axon(nm)" the same in nm. The g-ratio column is consistent with the Methods' definition.

The Fig. 4 script counts an ROI as changed when `ranksum` of its changes against a vector of zeros gives P < 0.05/nrois (nrois = 123), while the Methods and the Fig. 4b legend give a rank-sum test at "P < 0.01 with Bonferroni correction". The script's threshold reproduces the 69 and 44 ROIs of Supplementary Tables 1 and 2, whose largest listed P is 3.9e-4, above 0.01/122.
The Fig. 6a legend gives the PrePost x side x tract interaction as F(1,1238) = 6.02, P = 0.0025. The data give F = 6.02 and P = 0.0025 with 2 numerator df, as three tracts imply.

For fig6e-monkey-d-no-network-reduction, the paper does not say whether "the widespread reductions ... were not observed" in monkey D covers the control hemisphere. Its own Fig. 6e legend lists a significant control-side CEN difference, which the data show to be a decrease (P = 0.0089). The Methods list LIM without area 25, while the script and the legend's voxel counts include it. The authors could say which hemisphere the sentence refers to.

The dandiset's metadata names the paper only in its title, with no related resource, and gives no species, approach, measurement technique or variables measured. The sheets have no data dictionary beyond the legends inside some of them.

The seed connectivity tables hold one value per voxel and session, and the file names say "concatenated". The paper does not say whether a session's seed map was computed on concatenated runs or averaged over per-run maps, and no per-run maps are deposited.
The FigE1 script computes the foraging standard errors from column 2, the movement column (lines 91 to 96), so the error bars of the foraging plot in Extended Data Fig. 1 are those of movement.

Two scripts are deposited twice under two names with identical text (`Fig4 Fujimoto_NatNeuro_2026_FCmatrix.m` and `Fig4andE10C_Fujimoto_NatNeuro_2026_FCmatrix.m`; `Fig6DandE10D_dbs_FC_25norm_mkD_analysisscript_a.m` and `Fig6DandE10Ddbs_FC_25norm_mkD_analysisscript_a.m`).

entries.name: 001773-fujimoto-2026
entries.title: White matter remodeling and network changes after SCC-DBS in macaques (Fujimoto et al. 2026)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Fujimoto, Fujimoto, Elorette et al. (2026) on dandiset 001773, which holds the paper's derived values (voxel FA, voxel seed connectivity, group connectomes, CC1 and DAPI counts, EM g-ratios, home-cage behavior bins) and its MATLAB scripts. It repeats the paper's ANOVAs, Tukey-Kramer tests and rank-sum tests for the stimulated monkeys N and T, the lead-implanted monkey D and the nonsurgical controls. The whole-brain voxel maps and the controls' seed connectivity are not in the dandiset.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Fujimoto et al. (2026) from dandiset 001773

entries.name: 001785-fujimoto-2026
entries.title: White matter and network changes after subcallosal cingulate DBS in macaques (Fujimoto et al. 2026)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Fujimoto, Fujimoto, Elorette et al. (2026) on dandiset 001785, which holds per-session FA maps and normalized seed connectivity maps of two stimulated monkeys, one implanted control and three nonsurgical controls, with CC1 and DAPI immunofluorescence images and electron micrographs. Tract and ROI membership of voxels is taken from the paper's source data in DANDI:001773, and cells are counted from the images. The connectivity matrices and the hand-measured g-ratios cannot be tested from the dandiset.
